title: Drone frame to orthophoto geolocalization with LightGlue
summary: Matches a nadir drone frame against a georeferenced satellite or orthophoto tile with SuperPoint + LightGlue, fits a MAGSAC homography with OpenCV, and maps the frame centre through the GeoTIFF geotransform to lat/lon. The geometry (affine geotransform, homography mapping, WGS84 UTM, haversine) is a stdlib module with unit tests; the pipeline points at UAV-VisLoc, VPAIR and University-1652 for imagery and at hloc / AnyLoc for retrieval over large maps.
verified: geo_math.py and 12 unit tests ran with python3.14.7 stdlib on 2026-11-06. geolocalize.py ran on 2026-11-06 with torch 2.15.0 (CPU), LightGlue git 5a650c4, opencv-python 5.0.0.93, rasterio 1.5.2 on Python 3.12.14 against synthetic pairs cut from one public OpenAerialMap orthophoto (Tbilisi, CC-BY 4.0): 0.04-0.21 m error for yaw 0/60/135 deg, tilt and 60-150 m priors; 30.7 m error with 162 inliers when 40% of the frame was nodata at the ortho edge; a frame from a different city gave no fix (5 inliers). Frame and map come from the same survey, so this is a pipeline/geometry check, not a cross-season or real-UAV result; UAV-VisLoc/VPAIR/University-1652 were not run.
